reviewer_summary.question: Why must a newly chosen word go through processing, and which earlier calculations can each layer keep for reuse?
reviewer_summary.takeaway: Choosing blue uses the finished result for is; processing blue makes its own result, while separate layer caches let it reuse earlier keys and values.

findings.problem: Percent of the reading can mean a source’s fraction of the final sum, rather than a fraction taken of its source value.

resolution.note: All numerical share lines now explicitly say take this percentage of that source value.

findings.problem: Making The’s key again for is suggests fresh source preparation for each reader.

resolution.note: Explicitly revisit the existing The and sky keys and values; source preparation belongs to its position/layer.

findings.problem: Reading number is named before the multiplication creates its concrete instance.

resolution.note: Compute 1 times 0.8 first, then name the prepared reading number.

findings.problem: Source factor, arithmetic, key name and next multiplication arrive together.

resolution.note: Separate numerical preparation from key naming/job; also split query naming.

findings.problem: General base/extra parts recipe precedes one concrete match becoming parts.

resolution.note: Remove that general beat. First calculate 0.25 plus one, then name its sharing parts.

findings.problem: Sharing arithmetic is named before anything is shared.

resolution.note: Opening now declares simpler arithmetic and the scope without introducing sharing vocabulary.

findings.problem: Feed back could mean sending the calculated number rather than looking up the chosen word.

resolution.note: Closing explicitly says choose a piece, look it up as next input, process it, then choose.
